classification.difficultyReason: Construct the right-triangle model and use the equal distances to express both a leg and the hypotenuse with one variable.

content.prompt: A road runs in an east–west direction joining towns $A$ and $B$, which are $40\text{ km}$ apart. A third town, $C$, is situated $20\text{ km}$ due north of $B$. A straight road is built from $C$ to the road between $A$ and $B$ and meets it at $D$, which is equidistant from $A$ and $C$. Find the length of road $CD$.

answer.short:
$CD=25\text{ km}$.

Use $AD=CD$ and $DB=40-AD$ in right-angled triangle $DBC$.
answer.worked:
Let $AD=CD=x\text{ km}$. Then $DB=(40-x)\text{ km}$. Since $BC$ runs north and $DB$ runs east–west, triangle $DBC$ is right-angled at $B$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2&=(40-x)^2+20^2\\x^2&=1600-80x+x^2+400\\80x&=2000\\x&=25\end{align*}$$
Therefore $CD=25\text{ km}$.
